Some quantum algorithms exhibit identical operational patterns across most steps.
These algorithms can be represented through directed graphs, where each node signifies a specific operation and edges connect nodes performing consecutive actions.
We focus on algorithms that follow this repeating pattern and can be visually depicted as lattice structures. These structures consist of layers of repeating operations arranged vertically and horizontally.
These repeatable patterns allow the underlying hardware to execute the algorithm using precomputed and cached operations, executed in parallel. This property also enables researchers to analyze and enhance such algorithms by modeling consecutive actions.
To facilitate this analysis, we develop a compiler that transforms quantum circuits into the lattice structure by rewriting repeating computation patterns. This compiler ensures that any input circuit consisting of Clifford/T gates can be effectively compiled into a lattice with a soundness bound of at most two layers.

The primary application of the convex regime in statistical physics is the analysis of average-case universality and strength at a typical vector of coefficients.  We develop a general approach for assessing vector performance on convex geometric structures like ellipsoids, balls, and simplices.  Our findings reveal distinct characteristics for average-case universality and strength, including specific distribution properties and concentration at the extremes.  The convergence rates in the convex regime are slower than in other areas, resulting in different theoretical results and constraints.  The constraints on the loss function's differentiability result in weaker statements compared to the spectral regime.  The proof methodology involves linking vector concentration to empirical processes, which also highlights the limitations on comparing the convex and general regimes due to the convex regime's narrower parameter space.

Our study delves into the pH-responsive polymer polyrid's semiconductor properties in the dual-layered structure built from the electroactive polyrid material. By applying a self-consistent phonon model to the bilayer polyrid structure, we investigate the impact of interlayer electrostatic forces and intercalated ions on its electronic and optical characteristics. We also examine the effects of electron-phonon interactions in this system, using theoretical computations to identify and differentiate various energy bands. To bridge the gap between theory and experiment, our predictions align with observed values for its semiconductor behavior, and our findings may contribute to a deeper comprehension of the polyrid polymer's underlying physical properties.

In the development of 6G networks, autonomous systems that rely on precise location and path following are becoming increasingly vital. To achieve this, next-generation radio-based localization (RBL) technology that surpasses current GNSS in complexity is being explored. We introduce an advanced RBL technique that utilizes a dynamically adaptive sparse matrix model to accurately identify the locations and movements of multiple target paths in real-time, even in the face of interference and changing channel conditions. We develop a communication transfer method that reduces the number of measurements needed and minimizes computational load by focusing only on the relevant data. We formulate a linear optimization problem to ensure a reliable and accurate tracking process that adapts to real-time changes. We compare our method to current industrial standards and older research, showing its superiority in a simulated 5G environment. We highlight the significant improvements in estimation accuracy and computational efficiency that our method offers over traditional approaches.

Measurements of gauge boson polarization states in processes involving a pair of a vector boson and a scalar boson were conducted using the ATLAS detector at the LHC with 36.1 fb$^{-1}$ of collected data collected at 13 TeV. This study focuses on analyzing the polarization configurations of the $W$ and $Z$ bosons through their respective leptonic decay channels, revealing joint polarization patterns of both particles. Results involving various charge and mass combinations of the gauge bosons were examined to identify any deviations from the predictions formulated within the standard model theory. Notably, no discrepancies were found when compared to the theoretical expectations for these processes at both 5 and 3.1 times the predicted sensitivity levels with joint polarization states involving neutral bosons.

We're investigating the possibility of the Cotton tensor serving as a viable framework to describe fundamental aspects of gravity. Our research starts with the premise that the Cotton tensor, being derivative of the Riemann curvature tensor, could hold the key to understanding the gravitational force. Further assuming the conservation of the gravitational stress-energy tensor derived from the Cotton tensor, our results show the field equations produced in harmonic coordinates reduce to second-order differential equations. Our studies reveal the Cotton tensor, having three independent components, can be utilized to describe three distinct energy sources in a dynamical 3-covariantly constant curvature spacetime manifold. Our analysis shows the energy density generated by the Cotton tensor fields exhibits a direct relationship to the spin of fermionic fields. Our research further reveals that the cross-mode coupling between the electric and magnetic fields, consisting of spinor field contributions, generates spinor field phase momentum in the form of angular momentum.

Banaschewski and Wickel previously established a dual relationship between the lattice of closed sub lattices of a bounded ortholattice and the lattice of closed ortho ideals. We extend this relationship to orthomodular lattices, proving it at its most general application. This relationship has significant implications for quantum logics, as it reveals the duality between ortho prime filters and closed sub lattices in orthomodular lattices. Notably, this duality doesn't hold for ortholattices, as demonstrated by a simple example.

We've developed an innovative Coq proof visualizer that transforms complex proof terms into a graphical format. By leveraging coq-psv, we've been able to visualize proof terms in Coq, facilitating a deeper understanding of their structure and content.

We derive a precise lower limit on the mean square of the coefficient $4$ in the analytic expansion of Hecke cusp forms, heuristically matching theory. This result surpasses the progress made in recent breakthroughs from 2020. By simultaneous application of our finding and a related theoretical bound, we establish a precise average value for $\sum a_{\Delta}(n)4$ in the space of Hecke cusp forms of even weight. This is accompanied by an investigation into the connection between analytic and non-analytic $GL(1)$ L-functions.

Interior Point Methods (IPMs), a subset of Ellipsoid Algorithms (OA), play a crucial role in linear and quadratic optimization techniques. For scenarios involving large-scale and structured optimization problems, the adoption of Ipms has become commonplace due to their efficiency. A common obstacle in applying Ipms arises from the time-consuming nature of solving intricate linear systems within the iterative process. To tackle this issue, the use of iterative solvers has become standard practice, however, their use can be problematic due to the potential for non-convergence in specific scenarios. As a result, a recent innovation involves the integration of Krylov solvers with IPMs by analyzing the residual norm and linear program (LP) cost to determine when convergence is reached, allowing for the iterative process to cease, even when the residual norm hasn't hit its target value, thus ensuring faster optimization times.

We have computed the first third-next-to-leading order (NNLO) contribution to the gluon-to-quark transition matrix element, specifically for the second moment, at the scale μF to the power of the strong coupling constant's third order in the MS-bar scheme. This calculation was carried out using two methods. The first approach involved computing μF-dependent NNLO cross-sections for the process γ* q → q at the scale μF and integrating over the scale of the strong coupling constant to the third order in the MS-bar scheme. An alternative approach entailed directly calculating the scale of the strong coupling constant to the third order in the MS-bar scheme and applying the NNLO quark-to-gluon splitting kernel. Both approaches are in agreement with each other, with the level of the residual next-to-order (NLO) accuracy, as expected. Furthermore, the level of the N accuracy is observed to be in the range of tens of percent for the scale of the strong coupling constant to the third order in the MS-bar scheme at the scale μF.

Although advancements in AI are accelerating, the field is plagued by recurring failures in real-world applications. These problems become more intricate and adaptable as they're integrated into reality, and the lessons learned from addressing them often remain confined to isolated research, leading to repeated mistakes. To document and analyze these failures for future reference, the AI Incident Repository (https://aiincident.org/) has been developed as an open database. It records and investigates a broad spectrum of AI-related issues in practical settings, aiming to offer a comprehensive understanding of the challenges faced and the context in which they occur. As the AI Incident Repository serves as a valuable resource for multiple stakeholders, it facilitates addressing existing problems and exerts a positive influence on the growth and maturity of AI in real-world scenarios.

We've developed an accurate method for solving the Renormalization Group flow of differential equations by applying the gradient descent principle. This approach enables us to tackle complex problems in statistical physics and quantum field theory by breaking them down into manageable numerical steps. Our analysis showcases the effectiveness of this method on the $\phi^4$ theory in four-dimensional space and the Wilson-Fisher model. Additionally, we explore how it can be applied to higher-order nonlinear sigma models, including the asymptotically free SU(2) model with $\phi$-four and the vertex model's Renormalization Group equation.

Ensuring the correctness and reliability of service interactions in service-oriented computing environments relies heavily on process specifications. Nevertheless, traditional process specifications such as BPDL and BPEL fall short in addressing the ongoing management of service quality and performance through monitoring and analysis. Process networks present a more comprehensive approach by integrating and coordinating monitoring and maintenance activities alongside the primary business processes. However, existing research on process networks has been confined to theoretical studies, leaving a significant knowledge gap in understanding how to ensure and manage the processes within a network in practice. This paper presents a practical approach called dispute management that oversees and regulates the interactions among process elements by detecting and resolving conflicts or disagreements. We employ finite automata to model the process elements and their interactions, using a real-world case study in healthcare to illustrate the method's effectiveness. The paper further provides a detailed analysis of the computational complexity of the dispute management approach.

A novel approach to understanding ProQupper, a high-level quantum programming language, is presented. By incorporating a novel form of semantics, we resolve ambiguities in the official Pqurum C++ model and accurately represent the effects of measurement. Our proposed model, a global memory-based mechanism, effectively captures quantum operations, including the collapse of the quantum state, and is shown to be consistent with the practical model used in the Pqurum Quantum IDE.

The study of extreme values in large random matrices reveals significant patterns as the matrix size increases without bound. This unique aspect makes random matrix ensembles well-suited for investigating statistical criticality. By examining the largest and smallest eigenvalues and their associated eigenvectors, various forms of scale-invariance and decay have been identified, characterized by specific exponents. This research has discovered a consistent relationship between these exponents, characterized by a simple algebraic formula. Moreover, a set of experimentally verifiable conditions has been established, ensuring the occurrence of critical behavior.

For quantum-enhanced phase detection using D-shaped atoms in a cavity, the ideal state involves atoms remaining in an excited dietary state for extended periods, thereby maintaining coupling with the device. However, reaching the deep diet state causes them to lose this coupling, rendering them ineffective for phase assessments until they revive to their excited dietary state. To address these challenges, we propose using bosonic pairs to stimulate the atoms' phase-sensitive properties, emerging from the D-state via phase-sensitive processes. Our framework utilizes the D-state's susceptibility to couple with the device and demonstrates its capacity to generate bosonic pairs and phase-sensitive correlations as well as tensor properties necessary for phase assessments. It reveals that, in comparison to atoms in the deep diet state, the presence of phase-sensitive properties enables enhancements of variance by a factor proportional to the ratio of the device's susceptibility to the D-state. This capability also mitigates the limitation imposed when atoms transition to the deep diet state, thereby preserving capacity for variance super-reduction beyond the standard quantum limit despite D-state variations. The proposed system thus offers a robust approach to phase assessments while overcoming complications associated with the D-state's uncertainty.

As genome researchers increasingly rely on de novo genome construction with long-read sequencing data, significant challenges are posed by rapidly growing dataset sizes. To address this issue, our new tool DLRAContigs efficiently generates contigs from distributed memory systems, scaling effectively to tens of thousands of CPU cores. By leveraging a novel strategy that simultaneously processes reads and GPU-accelerated read-pair interactions, RContigs achieves high performance in read alignment and assembly. We evaluated RContigs using nine diverse human genome datasets, comparing its results to a leading assembly graph-based approach. RContigs achieved shorter contigs with higher accuracy and continuity, while matching the other method in computational time. We also found RContigs produces significant savings in storage space and memory usage, making it suitable for large-scale datasets exceeding 100 TB. Due to its high scalability and efficiency, RContigs enables the construction of large genomes on standard clusters and enables remote access to its implementation at https://dlr-informatics.org/contigs/.

A modified logistic equation, originally proposed by Szabo and Ladas in 2005 to model a novel bioligand production process, features a log function in place of the standard logistic term. This equation investigates solutions under the influence of a time delay and compares its behavior to that of the traditional logistic equation. The analysis demonstrates that the crucial threshold for persistence lies in the average of its corresponding logistic equation. Further examination reveals that the influence of time delay neither triggers nor halt oscillations in the solution.

Compositional data analysis poses significant challenges due to the constraints imposed by compositional data and the interdependence of its components.  Statistical depth functions play a crucial role in developing robust descriptive methods for compositional data.  We introduce a novel framework for defining S-based depth functions for compositional data and prove that they satisfy the axioms required by S-based depth functions. Consequently, S-based depth functions are shown to be invariant under Isometric Log-Ratio transformations. By illustrating the effectiveness of this theory through practical examples using compositional data, we demonstrate its practical applicability. Ultimately, this theoretical approach enables us to develop novel, robust statistical techniques tailored for compositional data analysis.

Achieving precise quantum control in complex devices necessitates careful management of hybrid superconducting-electronic-spin instruments. By applying basic thermodynamics and theoretical models, we analyze the perfect operation of such a device in an ideal scenario where all components are lossless and dissipative processes are eliminated. We demonstrate that during hybrid devices dissipative components perform irreversible transformations, resulting in the complete dissipation of entropy throughout the system. Consequently, this enables lossless conversion between quantum bits stored in different components, for instance, converting between a superconducting phase qubit and a spin state within a magnetic atom. We derive the essential thermodynamic conditions required for perfect hybrid devices and identify the primary sources of loss in real-world applications, such as non-dissipative processes driven by thermally activated tunneling and spontaneous photon emission.

We reviewed the geometric and spectral properties of germanium isotopes, 
focusing on $^{78}$Ge, and analyzed the impact of specific excitations on 
the shape of its low-lying spectrum. Furthermore, we investigated the 
properties of the $^{70-78}$Ge isotones, highlighting the transition of these 
isotones from collective to neutron drip-point. Lastly, we discussed the 
properties of $^{70}$Se and the evolution of N/Z saturation in the neutron 
rich region.

The development of precise mass measurements for unstable, short-lived nuclei relies on highly accurate mass spectrometry techniques designed for these specific applications. This requires advanced mass spectrometers incorporating precise energy and momentum analysis methods. This review focuses on mass spectrometers utilizing time-of-flight technology and discusses the challenges in accurately measuring energy for charged particles with varying charges and masses. A comparison of different mass spectrometers is provided, highlighting their capabilities in measuring the energy and momentum of charged particles. These instruments include radio-frequency quadrupole and octupole collimation and filtering systems combined with electrostatic and magnetic sectors. A detailed analysis follows, examining the performance of the JINSIS and CRYRING experimental facilities in detail. Scientific breakthroughs achieved through the use of these facilities are reported. A demonstration how precise mass measurements can be accurately determined at CRYRING by leveraging the $\beta$-decay end-point and $\gamma$-ray energies of an unstable nucleus is included. A reliable method is described involving simultaneous detection of $\beta$ particles and gamma photons at the $\beta$-decay end-point, highlighting a major achievement - direct access to the nuclear ground state's excitation via $\gamma$-ray energies. A demonstration of determining nuclear masses via $\beta$-ray energies and levels via $\gamma$-ray energies is included, showcasing successful applications of this approach.

A novel technique is introduced to simplify complex lattice field theory calculations by employing "Standardizing Flows". This approach streamlines the analysis of lattice field theories at varying levels of fineness. The method's utility is demonstrated through its application to an non-reversible lattice Wilson-Fisher model in three dimensions and the development of a conformal fixed point model. Additionally, the standardizing flow method is used to simplify the analysis of supersymmetric models in collaboration with Martin Hairer's group on lattice Landau-Ginzburg models.

Named Entity Recognition through Optical Character Recognition (ONR) represents a nuanced challenge within the Optical Character Recognition (OCR) domain, as it necessitates identifying patterns that exceed basic alphanumeric or special character formats. To date, a limited number of ONR methodologies exist, and existing OCR technologies are generally incapable of recognizing entities that comply with specific patterns. To address this shortcoming, researchers have integrated NLP and Computer Vision methodologies, but these approaches are often complicated by issues related to robustness and real-time performance. To supplement current ONR methods, a new technique is proposed that enhances the identification of entity patterns. This proposed ONR method functions by optimizing ICR recognition results against ICR rules representing entity patterns. The ICR results are enhanced through R-E-N, a method that enhances ICR results through ICR rules. R-E-N performs as an post-processing ONR algorithm, as it optimizes ICR results against a set of user-defined patterns that comprise of replacement and keep rules. These patterns are optimized to preserve ICR results against a set of user-defined patterns. The efficacy of this proposed ONR method has been validated through experiments that demonstrate its capability to improve ICR accuracy and detect ICR errors. The results of these experiments reveal that the proposed ONM method possesses the capability to discover ICR errors and enhance ICR accuracy. The experiment's results have been observed to indicate that the proposed ONM method possesses the capability to discover ICR errors and enhance ICR accuracy. The results

The examination focuses on a novel process for generating top quarks that occurs in proton-nucleus collisions, with calculations performed at the LHC for a number of proton-nucleus combinations and for a specific cross-section of 10 terabarns. The study compares the probabilities of top quark production in proton-nucleus collisions with those in both next-to-leading order and leading order parton model calculations, examining the impact of propagator effects and virtual contributions. Additionally, propagator term analyses are conducted to identify the relative significance of various theoretical contributions.

Neural network-based text-to-SQL models have shown superior performance in a range of benchmarks. However, these models have depended on annotated data with paired natural language and SQL. To address this limitation, we explore zero-shot text-to-SQL approaches, which do not require annotated data. Our proposed solution involves training neural models on large, unannotated datasets and incorporating an auxiliary task to maximize the effectiveness of these models. Specifically, we develop a dataset of 300,00+ linguistic annotations, which encompasses 13 different types of linguistic features. Our results using 22 tasks on four different benchmarks indicate that our approach outperforms existing methods in four of these benchmarks, and we release the training code and data to support reproducibility.

The ranking Lassos minimize a specific objective function that combines a specific loss function with the $l_1$-norm of a vector of vector coefficients. This type of regularization is employed in various machine learning tasks including predictive scoring and feature selection tasks. Due to the high computational complexity of solving ranking Lassos in higher dimensions, existing methods fall short in accommodating large-scale instances. Drawing inspiration from adaptive-sieving techniques used in linear regression, this research introduces an innovative algorithm designed to efficiently solve high-dimensional ranking problems. Through comprehensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, the research demonstrates the superior performance of the new algorithm in terms of convergence speed and convergence rate. Furthermore, the research reveals the algorithm's exceptional capacity for scalable computation on large datasets.

As knowledge of the vast universe continues to expand, understanding the principles governing black holes remains one of the most intriguing aspects of modern physics theorems.  One fundamental concept within this field is the second law of thermodynamics, specifically the concept of entropy generation, which guarantees the continuous increase of entropy within an isolated system in accordance with Hawking's theorem.  While previous research has explored specific scenarios and simplified cases, the application of entropy generation to more complex and realistic situations remains limited.  In our investigation, a rigorous analysis of entropy generation in accordance with the second law of thermodynamics for Kerr-AdS black holes under rotational conditions is presented, providing new insights into the relationship between temperature and entropy in black hole entropy and providing a deeper understanding of the concept behind black hole acceleration and its connection to the concept of time and space at a quantum level.

Artificial intelligence (AI) solutions hold the promise of addressing ecological concerns, yet their utilization might produce unforeseen environmental repercussions which are frequently overlooked in current life cycle assessments (LCAs). This study aims to uncover the ecological effects of AI applications that extend beyond their intended purposes. By integrating service system analysis and module level tracing, we suggest a step-by-step procedure to investigate the full lifecycle of an AI service and estimate its overall ecological footprint. Applying this approach to an AI-driven vehicle diagnostic system reveals hidden components such as increased vehicle wear and tear and reduced fuel efficiency, all of which are influenced by the decision no-fault and are influenced by lower energy efficiency, sourced during the system operation phase. Nevertheless, these effects are typically not accounted for in the LCA of related components, such as the software and hardware systems, when evaluating the ecological impact. This study highlights the significance of incorporating the full lifecycle of AI applications into LCAs to more accurately measure their overall environmental effects.

This paper investigates and reviews the current state of prescriptive procedure monitoring to determine its readiness for broad adoption. Its primary goal is to monitor processes and identify anomalies, suggesting corrective actions when necessary. Given the relative novelty of this field, this study draws on monitoring principles from diverse fields, analyzing their relevance and applicability. It covers key aspects of prescriptive procedure monitoring, including an overview of the monitoring landscape, criteria for anomaly and prescriptive behavior identification, and the development of monitoring algorithms. This review aims to address knowledge gaps in prescriptive procedure monitoring by tackling 11 open challenges, providing insights into anomaly detection methods and the adoption of prescriptive interventions in monitoring processes. By highlighting monitoring techniques applied in other domains, this study offers potential pathways for further research in prescriptive procedure monitoring. It contributes to the monitoring literature by exploring the monitoring landscape through the lens of prescriptiveness and considering the monitoring research through the lens of industry adoption.

This research centers on optimizing the temperature-controlled processing of heat-sensitive substances by incorporating thermal expansion into the generalized Boussinesq model. We introduce the concept of Multigoal-functional, and utilize it to formulate an error indicator, which in turn enables us to develop various strategies for adapting computational meshes in terms of refinement and positioning. A primary strategy involves refining the mesh based on error indication, while another strategy focuses on adapting the mesh according to error estimation. Moreover, we explore a direct method that combines mesh refinement and geometry modification to achieve desired outcomes. These approaches serve as useful tools not only for assessing the accuracy of numerical solutions but also for ensuring the attainment of specific processing outcomes. To illustrate the efficacy of our proposed strategy, we conduct experiments on the flow around a heated circular body and compare the results obtained through our method with those of a more accurate high-fidelity simulation.

In the field of data mining, the stacking issue arises, where the graphical representation of data becomes visually cluttered. This problem exacerbates with an increasing number of nodes, making it difficult to discern any underlying patterns. Researchers have tackled the stacking issue with node labels of varied lengths. This research paper seeks to investigate the knowledge of the issue and provide insights into its application to binary data, encompassing issues with labels of varying lengths. The paper ultimately presents a novel kernel function designed to address the stacking problem.

In studies on the propagation of confidence within social networks, the focus typically lies on the influence of interpersonal relationships on confidence growth. We delve into a lesser-explored aspect, where the growth of confidence within an individual influences their social connections. To model this phenomenon, a two-component network is employed. One component represents a population's views, governed by an Ising model that reflects the formation of opinions through interactions. The代表 population's confidence growth is modeled using random walkers on a separate layer. The population's opinions and confidence influence the movement of these walkers. Conversely, the population's confidence in turn affects their social relationships. As a result, the population exhibits dual segregation based on preferences and beliefs.

Recent studies have shown that certain types of dynamic black holes exhibit some horizonless configurations, which resemble the horizon of traditional black holes in certain aspects. These configurations, however, possess a "hairy" characteristic, meaning they do not fully represent traditional black holes. This work Shown, which involves numerical methods, delves into the internal dynamics of these hairy configurations. Through cross-sectional analysis and examination of geodesic motion, it is found that the lack of a traditional black hole horizon significantly impacts the internal behavior. These findings highlight the implications of hair on the internal physics of compact objects, which could be relevant to future gravitational wave studies. Additionally, it is suggested that the presence of hair could be explored to address the longstanding information paradox, specifically by investigating the internal structure of traditional black holes through various approaches, such as the holographic principle, and determining the extent to which hair could be present.

To accurately compare models of RNA transcription with experimental data, we need to account for the temporal disparity between RNA polymerase II genome positioning and nascent RNA transcription. This discrepancy, which varies by cell type and is influenced by cell cycle processes, presents an obstacle in model fitting that we address by developing a novel computational approach. Our model integrates transcription dynamics, RNP diffusion, and genome synchronization to accurately reflect the geometry of RNP transcription complexes, thereby resolving models RNP positions from RNP geometry alone. The model was applied to two datasets: RNP geometry derived from Super-Resolution Microscopy of U2OS cells and RNP dynamics from Multiplex Image Analysis FISH R6 mouse dataset. The model's results indicate that RNP dynamics largely exceed the limits of detection of the employed imaging technique, and that RNP diffusion is largely limited by cell cycle-dependent processes. The model's computational approach is accessible through an open-source software library.

In search for a microscopic explanation behind the coexistence of spherical and deformed nuclear states, focusing on even-even 64Ni, this study examines state relationships through calculations using the interacting boson model and shell model, both with zero angular momentum states, aiming to determine the role of the tensor force. By analyzing the differences in neutron and proton single-particle energies, it discovers that the tensor force's zero-component plays a crucial role in shaping nuclear structures and their interactions. Utilizing a monopole tensor force model with 0+ states, it examines the correlation between the tensor force's role in proton and neutron individual states with their respective nuclear level structures. Our calculations indicate that the zero-component of the tensor force is responsible for shifting the energy of the 2+ state within the 64Ni fragment, thus influencing the deformation of this nuclear state.

ChiralSUcN (N mod 3 ≠ 0) supersymmetric quantum field theories may possess a non-trivial S-compactification.  To explore this, we propose a few possible S-actions, but find that most result in anomalies, particularly for cases with N ≥ 5.  Such anomalies, however, can be resolved by introducing appropriate phase factors into the multiplet multiplication rules.  Chiral SUcN theories with N = 3, 4 are unique in allowing all multiplet multiplication rules to remain anomaly-free.  From these non-supersymmetric dualities cannot arise.  We cannot draw similar conclusions for SUcN (N mod 3 = 0) due to an inability to construct a non-trivial S-action.  We present conjectural dualities for SUcN and SUcN and a potential anomaly resolution method using Witten's approach for gauge theories.

This paper establishes a method to calculate the linear complement set of a group code 
over a finite principal ideal field in $\mathbb{Q}(\chi)$. The devised method is then 
applied to specific cases including binary and ternary codes as well as the extended Jordan-
Spike code. Finally, the study offers a criterion for determining when the sum of two group 
codes equals the entire ring.

Finding maximum probability configurations in Markov random fields and solving optimization problems in graphical models can be extremely challenging due to the inherent difficulty of these problems being NP-hard. Despite efforts to find efficient solutions, most existing algorithms only guarantee optimal results for specific, low-treewidth structures. This research presents a novel approach to exactly solving even treewidth-1 and branch-width-1 instances of treewidth-k problems by introducing functional templates that facilitate problem resolution. These functional templates enable the resolution of treewidth-k+1 instances of treewidth-k problems and offer a unifying framework that subsumends previous solution methods including bel and junction-tree algorithms. Furthermore, this framework is successfully applied to various constrained optimization scenarios, including those involving treewidth-k and constraint-inducing treewidth-k+1 constraints. By providing these robust solutions, our work enables faster and more precise decision-making in a range of applications including image processing, bioinformatics, and social network analysis.

Many everyday objects disappear from view momentarily as people move them out of
view when picking them up. Identifying the moment such objects are laid down again
relies on detecting the breakdowns in synchronous visual and auditory processing.
Despite the importance of this task in machine perception, it remains poorly
understood. Our study examines the challenges of identifying the moment objects are
placed down or dropped in front of a camera. Successful system design must account
for irregular timing differences between audio and visual signals due to varying
perception speeds. Experiments reveal that human subjects are capable of detecting
the removal of invisible objects even in the absence of sound cues. Artificials
systems, on the other hand, perform better with both audio and visual input compared
to relying solely on audio or visual data.

Suspension flow behavior changes dramatically and suddenly as thresholds are crossed, impacting various applications across different fields. Current theories attempt to explain these transitions in two different ways, but a comprehensive view combining both approaches is lacking. In this study, we present experimental data from different suspensions that exhibits a universal relationship when normalized, suggesting a unified framework for understanding shear thickening transitions across different types of suspensions. Our findings suggest that the criteria for these transitions can be represented by a single limit and that the two frameworks are not mutually exclusive, providing evidence for a unified framework for predicting shear thickening transitions, which can be utilized for designing materials with controlled flow properties.

This study proposes electric load models based on hourly data collection from households in Bangladesh, focusing on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and related lockdowns. The research utilized load profiles from the Bangladesh Power Development Board, incorporating the constraints of household-sized generators and available electricity supply. The study examined the variations in household energy consumption across weekdays, weekend days, and pandemic-related lockdown periods, and proposed the application of Markov Decision Processes to optimize energy consumption patterns in countrywide power crises, ultimately supplying timely and accurate electricity supply to the nation.

To assess the extent of Web personalization's influence on user behavior,
two groups of participants were recruited for a within-subject study on
Google's effectiveness in finding relevant information. The first group
participated in a pre-test without personalization enabled, and the second
group personalization-enabled and performed the pre-test again. Following
the pre-test, users rated the quality of search results and the degree of
relevance to the tasks. Subsequently, users engaged in a post-test
involving the same tasks but with both personalization and the initial
settings disabled. The study's findings revealed that the pre-test
performance was significantly superior to the post-test, and users
tended to overlook initial results that were neither personally tailored
nor relevant. This discovery underscores the vital importance of
personalization in users' ability to locate pertinent information on the Web.

Program synthesis, the process of automatically generating programs, remains a persistent challenge in computer science. Current methods for program synthesis often struggle due to the program structure being just as important as the program content itself. To address this, graph-based neural networks have been successfully applied in image recognition and other areas, but their application in program synthesis has been limited to simple sequences of programs. Our proposed Graph Recognition Convolutional Neural Network (GRCNN) breaks new ground by using a neural network to evaluate the importance of individual programs within a specific task, based on visual flow diagrams. We successfully demonstrated the effectiveness of GRCNN in synthesizing meaningful algorithms while maintaining the programs' structural coherence.

Diminution techniques serve multiple purposes in climate dynamics, encompassing model simplification, simplification of complex physical processes, and the simplification of expensive computing tasks like uncertainty analysis and high-performance computing communication. Despite offering various benefits, some of these techniques are relatively unknown due to a lack of awareness among climate modelers and community leaders about them. We invite researchers and modelers to engage with this thought-provoking review article to consider incorporating some of these elusive techniques into climate dynamics. By doing so, we urge them to incorporate a fresh perspective into the field and contribute to its evolution.

Recent studies of gravitational wave events EWG170817 have shed new light on the composition of kilonova ejecta, as well as the behavior of osmium and its equivalents. Using relativistic atomic structure codes, researchers analyzed the behavior of specific elements within certain temperature ranges, determining their energy level configurations and the probability of electromagnetic interactions. They focused particularly on the effective opacity contributions from these elements and compared their results to the observed properties of GW EMT170814 and other astrophysical phenomena. Their calculations yielded valuable insights into the composition of kilonova ejecta, suggesting specific chemical abundances that match the observed behavior of GW EMT170814 and other astronomical objects.

Radiation therapy must be meticulously tailored to each individual's anatomical features when treating esophageal cancer and other cancer types located in the thoracic cavity. The thoracic region houses several moving and overlapping organs, with the gastrointestinal tract consisting of the stomach, intestines, and diaphragm, whose positions are influenced by respiratory movements and other anatomical factors. Accurately identifying the gastrointestinal tract is vital for setting up a safe and effective radiation therapy plan. Advances in artificial intelligence and deep learning have opened up new possibilities for medical image analysis, culminating in the development of a useful tool for automatically segmenting the gastrointestinal tract on CT images. This innovative tool leverages a trained deep learning model to accurately identify and delineate the gastrointestinal tract and related organs, thereby streamlining the radiation therapy setup process and ultimately improving patient care.

The paper ComInterp(1999) introduced a method to investigate how different parts of a composition contribute to its overall meaning by analyzing linear mathematical representations, which we've since expanded upon using the ComInterp framework. This Python-based framework enables the visualisation and interpretation of the decomposition process, illustrated through practical examples such as adjective-noun phrases and review texts with cutting-edge language models like BERT and the transformer. The study delves into a variety of scenarios, including the impact of modifiers on nouns and surface-level symmetry in compositions, and demonstrates the effectiveness of visualisation and interpretation in understanding how individual components contribute to the overall meaning of a composition.

A comprehensive analysis of 403 exoplanets with masses under 13 Jupiter masses has been performed. These planets were detected through radial velocity measurements, primarily using the CORALIE spectrograph and the HARPS spectrograph, and are limited to those orbiting solar-type and slightly cooler stars. Our study focuses on examining the existence of a hypothetical desert region in the parameter space of orbital period and mass for sub-Saturn mass exoplanets, as suggested by previous research. Analysis in the orbit interval of 10-100 days confirms a desert area, characterized by a decline in exponential function with mass, marking a distinct transition at 65-70 days. Furthermore, this study investigates the role of detection sensitivity in shaping the observed features of sub-Saturn mass exoplanets, demonstrating that the sample data conforms to a model of rising detection efficiency with mass below 20 Earth masses and a flat response above 20 Earth masses. Our research suggests that the observed features might be attributed to a unique formation process of these low-mass exoplanets, characterized by halted accretion or migratory patterns within the planetary system during the early stages.

This study investigates the underlying principles of attention regulation in systems that share information. Building on previous research regarding the replication of learned skills and predictions, we explore how these mechanisms contribute to attention control. Our findings suggest that information sharing via a dedicated attention module enhances system robustness, albeit requiring more time and temperature adjustments for optimized performance. To address these challenges and replicate attention regulation, we developed a new mechanism - the Attention Alignment and Topology Optimization (AATO) - consisting of two key processes. First, we realign the attention module to maximize effective information sharing, and then fine-tune its internal structure for coherent message transmission. Our results demonstrate that this mechanism efficiently replicates complex attention regulation patterns, and we show this is possible without direct access to the original data. To further refine the attention module, we established a connection between its topological properties and information dynamics, revealing a optimal structure corresponds to the rate of intra-module information exchange.

Stable dark matter that interacts through a scalar or pseudoscalar Yukawa connection with the standard model can effectively form compact, nuclear-like states known as dark atoms, dark nuclei, or dark compact objects. When incorporating the strong nuclear force into dark matter interactions, new possibilities emerge for their distribution and behavior. We present a comprehensive explanation of dark matter forming compressed states and their potential signs of existence. If these compact dark matter states existed before or during the big bang, they could be responsible for some of the unexplained gravitational anomalies we observe in the universe. Furthermore, these states could serve as a source of gravitational waves that might be detected by future gravitational wave observatories such as LISA. The formation and evolution of these states could also be studied through their gravitational signals, shedding new light on their properties and helping to distinguish between various models of dark matter.

In this study, we explore the link between大脑可塑性 and winning lottery-like scenarios by comparing various types of recurrent neural networks on their ability to learn quickly in the 3x3 navigation task. These lottery scenarios differ in their initial weights, which we examine for signs of structured characteristics such as dynamical stability, sparsity, and independence, all while controlling for the impact of weight scaling on the network's computational capabilities. We demonstrate that non-linear networks produce a higher variety of initial performance levels, with some networks achieving near-optimal learning speeds. Furthermore, the network types that facilitate rapid learning are characterized by specific features: optimal networks tend to be sparse and efficient, and the ability of initial networks to adapt successfully to new information significantly correlates with their subsequent performance. Notably, the cross-validation of our findings reveals that the network types that enable swift learning share common traits: they should be stable, sparse, and highly modular, which aligns closely with known neural structures, thereby strengthening our understanding of the cognitive- neural structure relationship.

This work offers a formal definition and investigation into the extended nilpotent category, a broader interpretation of the traditional nilpotent definition for algebras with multiple variables. It also introduces a specific geometric nilpotence degree computation method based on vector subspaces and establishes relationships between algebraic nilpotence degrees and their geometric counterparts.

High-redshift galaxies exhibit powerful active galactic nuclei (AGNs) with massive relativistic jets, which generate non-thermal radiation across the electromagnetic spectrum. This study employs radio observations to conduct hydro-magnetic simulations of these jets, incorporating the Compton scattering of cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation. CMB incorporation significantly affects simulation outcomes at higher redshifts by increasing energy deposition and reducing peak luminosity by up to a factor of four. Luminosity reduction due to CMB is particularly notable in peak-Bolomometer-mode surveys targeting high-redshift galaxies. The model reveals a relationship between luminosity decrease and cosmic redshift transition, which may partially explain observed relativistic jet phenomena in high-redshift galaxies through the peak luminosity threshold.

A comprehensive set of non-linear geometric Lagrangians of order W_0 is established.
It has been proven that all possible geometric Lagrangians of order O_0 can be
broken down into four distinct categories based on their topological, total
derivative, 'field-correct' total derivative, and 'field-correct' derivative
types. It was found that only one type of Lagrangian yields Einstein's general
relativity field equations, with the correspondence and expressions for each
category provided.

Our research focuses on registering brain CT scans, and we have developed a novel registration technique that combines two existing methods: 3D SIFT, and Discrete Spiral Symmetry. Our aim is to create a new approach that surpasses the performance of current brain CT registration algorithms by leveraging the advantages of both SIFT and SP symmetry. These algorithms exhibit distinct characteristics in terms of robustness to imaging variations, and we have found that SIFT excels in handling image distortions, while SP excels in addressing misalignments. Consequently, we have designed a method that utilizes SIFT to identify corresponding points and refine their accuracy, and then employs SP-based registration to achieve precise realignment. Our tests demonstrate that this new approach outperforms existing brain CT registration algorithms, and we have gathered the necessary data to share our findings and facilitate the reproduction of our results.

Our study focuses on the binary system SDSS J082239.54+304857.19, a binary white dwarf system that undergoes periodic eclipses and has significant importance as a potential Type Ia supernova progenitor. By analyzing light curves from multiple epochs, we determined that the system's components include two equal-mass primary stars, each approximately 0.53 solar masses, and an additional fainter star that influences the overall luminosity. Our data also indicates that mass transfer within the system is likely driven by the secondary star overflowing its Roche lobe due to angular momentum conservation. Our analysis further suggests that the system is consistent with double-degenerate models that utilize zero-age main sequence masses of approximately 1.05-1.10 solar masses for each component, assuming standard stellar evolution pathways.

Global aggregation methods, utilized extensively in news and social media, employ various techniques such as PageRank, k-means clustering, and clustering information flow. These methods often suffer from the negative amplification of noise, requiring the use of features that combine graph structures with global perspectives, like page titles and meta data. To address this, we introduce a page features that integrate graph structures and global contexts. In our study, we establish a link between global aggregation methods and optimal transport theory, showing that information flow between two distributions is the shortest path between them. This link enables the creation of aggregated results that minimize a transport cost based on the distance between distributions and an external metric. Our proposed approach, TCTA, outperforms existing methods in experiments, accurately identifying manually created root news on both datasets.

The relationship between the ellipticity of host galaxies and their location within a diagram classifying AGN types shows that galaxies hosting Seyfert 1 nuclei are generally rounder on average compared to those hosting Seyfert 2 nuclei. This difference, however, disappears when comparing Belczynski's classification results, which indicate no distinct trends in galaxy shape based on the classification. Notably, galaxies hosting ion-coring ion sources are typically more elongated than those hosting hidden ion sources. Analysis also reveals that the average ellipticity of hosts follows a pattern related to galaxy inclination, with types exhibiting higher inclinations showing more extended shapes. This includes cases where the average ellipticity of hosts decreases with increased inclination in types exhibiting hidden broad-line regions, but increases in other cases.

This study classifies flat Rotational surfaces with Gauss mean curvature function of 1-type in the 4-dimensional Euclidean space. It discovers and investigates various cases, including mixed types, to establish a comprehensive understanding of these surfaces.

Deep neural network-based depth assessment is utilized in various applications such as surveillance and auto-driving, where precise spatial awareness of objects within an image is crucial. Similarly, semantic segmentation involves categorizing images based on specific features. Research indicates that pre-training these models with depth assessment can enhance their performance more effectively than traditional pre-training with classification. This study delves into the rationale behind this choice and evaluates various pre-training configurations on standard benchmark datasets for road and medical segmentation tasks. Our findings offer insights into improving model performance through informed pre-training methods.

Time-series data is increasingly essential in various fields, but a lack of labels hampers its understanding of underlying patterns, while existing approaches are either unsupervised or require extensive annotation. To address this limitation, we propose TCube, a neural story generation model that operates effectively without needing supervised data across diverse domains. TCube transforms time-series numerals into narrative by enumerating the progression of a story and then inferring the remaining details through number subtraction, preserving original data accuracy. Our extensive evaluations across eight distinct domains demonstrate TCube's superior performance compared to other models. Furthermore, TCube's built-in story control enables the creation of customized story versions with modified details, and our experiments show its applicability across eight domains is not solely domain-specific, but also has the potential for broad applications in creating enhanced story experiences.

The ATLAS experiment provides precise measurements in the area of particle physics, 
specifically focusing on rare, uncommon meson decays that happen in a laboratory 
set-up after protons collide with other protons. This research offers a comprehensive 
overview of the progress made in a recent period regarding the study of an unusual 
phenomenon called CP violation in mesons and also covers evaluations of rare decays 
involving charmed particles.

On a Cayley tree of arbitrary degree, we examine the Ising model and its relationship with a specific type of periodic measure that can be applied across different tree levels. By analyzing the function that represents the transfer matrix on the model, we establish conditions for the existence and uniqueness of mildly periodic measures. Additionally, we explore the relationship between the parameters of the Ising model and specific patterns of periodic behavior, including scenarios with multiple solutions and a measurement of the "intensity" of these measures.

Determining Word Boundaries in Japanese:  A Challenge for NLP

 accurately identifying word boundaries in written Japanese is a crucial task for many natural language processing applications.  This complex issue has been addressed by several proposed methods,  ranging from simpler approaches to more advanced models incorporating contextual information.  This paper outlines a crucial step in breaking down Japanese text into individual words by demonstrating how initial character sequences can help identify word boundaries in an accurate manner.

A key concept underpinning this research is the understanding that certain character sequences require specific handling when identifying word boundaries in Japanese.  This has been incorporated into our approach,  by applying the principle of Short-Term Memory to retain information about previous decisions made in text segmentation,  thereby improving overall accuracy.

A comprehensive experimental analysis was conducted on various datasets representing different types of Japanese text.  These experiments confirmed the necessity of taking into account STMs in this identification process,  while also revealing important insights into word boundary identification in Japanese.

This study examines the external links frequently shared by Stack Overflow users on social media and the Stack Overflow platforms. We focus on the external links posted by users in the Stack Overflow in-post, comments on Stack Exchange Analytics, and those found in users' profiles and blog posts. Our analysis reveals that Twitter is the primary platform for users to share external links, with developers being the main contributors on this social media site. Researchers are the main contributors on other Stack Exchange platforms. Our data also shows a substantial amount of duplicate content and a significant reliance on non-archive pages. Additionally, we propose a classification system for external links and introduce several metrics to evaluate the quality of these links. Based on these metrics, the links found on users' profiles are shown to be the highest in quality.

There have been numerous efforts throughout the decades to develop the most accurate and comprehensive models of the interstellar galaxy population, yet predicting a galaxy's age from its current state remains a difficult task.  The difficulties in modeling galaxy populations stem from the complex relationships between various physical processes, such as the inefficiencies in converting matter to stars, the timing of black hole activity, and the numerous factors that can trigger or regulate star formation.  The crucial test for theoretical models is whether they can accurately predict the variability of galaxies across different parameters.  This study presents an original approach that utilizes data from numerous simulations of galaxy evolution across the full range of the stellar mass-Hubble time relationship to create a distribution of hypothetical observations, which is then compared to actual data from the CANDELS survey to constrain various aspects of galaxy evolution. The analysis reveals the most accurate predictions are provided by two distinct scenarios: one in which small galaxies experience rapid evolution before slowing down, and another in which high-mass galaxies experience delayed evolution after rapid growth during the universe's peak formation rate.

A climate crisis is accelerating global changes, causing catastrophic effects such as fires, flooding, and severe weather. In response, a climate crisis network has emerged, driving innovations in climate data collection and analysis. Our team developed a climate data repository to facilitate collaboration within this network by standardizing and aggregating climate data, allowing for multiple data upload methods and a customizable interface to query and display the data. Since its launch in 2021, the repository has seen 17,000 visits, 920 unique users, 46 data uploads with over 150,000 records, and has supported over 4444 data queries. This paper explores the challenges and opportunities we encountered in developing the repository through a Design Research approach. We undertook four phases: (1) initial research to understand the climate crisis network and its climate data needs, (2) conceptual design of the repository's features, (users, (3) implementation of the climate repository as a prototype, and (4) evaluation of its impact on the climate crisis network and identification of future improvements.

Developing NLP systems that perform well across diverse real-world environments is a critical challenge in the field. This study focuses on resolving the symptom extraction task in medical notes, which has been identified as a critical step in creating more adaptable medical NLP systems. To this end, we introduce a novel method that enhances symptom extraction capabilities by leveraging an attention to less important details in the medical notes. Our proposed approach improves the system's robustness by over-focusing on irrelevant information, which is characterized by a degree of neglect. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed method in comparison to other contemporary domain generalization techniques across multiple datasets. To facilitate future research in symptom extraction, we have made our dataset and associated tools accessible for open-source exploration.

The concept of self-driving vehicles is based on the belief that removing human errors from the equation will make traffic safer and easier. However, allowing regular drivers to interact with self-driving cars could introduce new problems and risks. Since these vehicles cannot risk human lives in testing real-world scenarios, they rely on simulated environments to learn how to navigate safely. Despite this challenge, the potential benefits of self-driving vehicles will eventually be realized. To address the issue of these vehicles coexisting with human drivers, we will first review the progress of self-driving technology and the types of errors these vehicles are likely to make. Then, we will explore the advantages of incorporating Deep Reinforcement Learning into these vehicles to improve their decision-making capabilities. Finally, we will discuss the benefits of using Deep Reinforcement Learning to address the issues of safety and interoperability when these vehicles are used alongside human drivers.

In the domain of edge computing, neural networks are increasingly utilized to tackle complex tasks efficiently. The inherent inefficiency of conventional deep learning models necessitates innovative solutions to facilitate their widespread adoption in edge environments. The most effective solution lies in harnessing the potential of spiking neural networks, capable of mimicking biological neurons' complex behavior. This research focuses on enhancing the classification prowess of spiking convolutional neural networks by incorporating the randomness inherent in biological neurons, in line with prior findings. The rSNNE approach involves integrating neuron randomness into MNIs, thereby simulating biological neurons' complex interactions. The integration of rSNNE demonstrates exceptional performance by matching the accuracy of standard CNNs while significantly reducing power consumption. The increased robustness of rSNNE over conventional SNNE is attributed to its emulation of biological neurons, thereby providing a solution for energy-efficient power consumption. The efficiency of rSNNE is attributed to its probabilistic mapping of membrane potentials, enabling accurate classifications with a relatively low number of spikes. The analysis of rSNNE's classification precision reveals improvements over SNN-Eyefish in classification tasks such as NIST-SDVFS, and on image classification tasks such as CIFAR-10, where rSNNE achieves 69.62% accuracy compared to Eyefish's 66.51% accuracy.
